policy: A launcher-shaped script is one outside runtime/ember-lab and tools/ember-cli that is directly runnable and creates a child process for a run. Issue 898 removes that class from the tree: the daemon is the only way a run starts. Every path below is enumerated with the exact bytes adjudicated; editing one changes its digest and re-opens it for review.

exceptions.reason: public-command interpreter adapter. It launches only the exact receipt-bound Python interpreter selected by docs_information_system.py, with hidden/no-window process creation and redirected standard streams; it does not select or dispatch a training run.

run body, not a launcher. This is the program the daemon dispatches as its caged child; its __main__ is how the daemon starts it, and the child processes it creates are its own workers inside the same job object. Deleting its entry point would delete the run itself.
run body, same standing as run_vertical_slice.py: dispatched by the daemon, spawns only its own workers inside the cage.
matched on its name, not its behaviour. It is a CLI parity harness: the child it creates is the packaged CLI under test with a 20-second timeout, never a training run.
matched on its name, not its behaviour. It adapts the roadmap runner to a file-backed JSON transport; the child it creates is that runner, never a training run.

genuine hermetic deployment fixture. It creates fake application and runtime executables and invokes the installer only inside a unique temporary repository/install root; it never starts a training run or a production cockpit. The exact digest is required because filename-based test exclusions are forbidden.

preparation-only build helper. It may invoke the pinned Bun package/build commands and Cargo compiler, but it never starts Ember.exe, ember-lab serve, or any training run; its only production outputs are immutable application/runtime paths consumed by the governed cockpit command.

hermetic unit test for the historical governed-run adapter. It creates a temporary worker fixture and exercises timeout, cancellation, manifest, and receipt behavior without addressing any production run or persistent custody root.
CPU-only wrapper test with CUDA explicitly disabled. Its child commands are temporary stub-core fixtures used to prove STOP/CEILING_STOP and receipt shapes; it does not launch a GPU job or daemon.

certified-launch orchestration unit suite. It loads the module under test into isolated temporary custody and substitutes owned test commands/mocks to verify closed arguments, cleanup, and receipt propagation; it is not a contributor-facing production entry.
custody-gate integration fixture. Its subprocess is the real ember-lab custody-verify CLI against isolated shard bytes and SQLite state, never the trainer or a training launch.

runner preflight unit suite that deliberately avoids allocating the production model. Any process surface is a patched or temporary probe used to test refusal ordering and preflight evidence, not a runnable training entry.

storage-preflight fixture operating on temporary checkpoint and custody paths. Its child-process cases exercise bounded runner storage diagnostics; they do not dispatch a model run or expose a production launcher.

canonical-launcher hermetic acceptance suite. It copies tools/launchers/Ember.cmd and preparation scripts to a unique temporary repository, uses fake Bun/ember-lab command files, and asserts governed argv and refusals without starting a real cockpit or training run.

offline nativization-motion test suite. It executes only synthetic temporary runner/import fixtures to validate delta and receipt calculations, with zero network and no production training identity or custody.

bootstrap compatibility row, temporary. This file is the AST scanner itself. The guard on this branch excludes its own scanner, but CI adjudicates with the base-pinned kernel, whose older line-oriented detector sees the scanner's own call-operator invocation of git and reports it as launcher-shaped. The exact digest admits only these reviewed bootstrap bytes and nothing else. Verified both ways: the base kernel refuses without this row and passes with it, and the branch kernel passes either way, treating the row as unused. Remove the row once the kernel CI pins is the successor that excludes the scanner by construction.

desktop installer, not a training launcher. It starts only the installed desktop application after copying the reviewed application/runtime bundle; it never selects or dispatches a model training run.
